definition: Rancor means deep, long-lasting bitterness or ill will.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word rancor. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know rancor should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Some rancor still seasons every casserole Aunt May brings to the reunion — forty years since the will was read, and Cousin Ed's portion is still the smallest.
Annoyance fades by dinner — nothing like rancor, which can outlive the quarrel that started it.
A grudge stores one grievance on one shelf; it stops short of rancor, bitterness spread deep and kept for years.

Bitterness is the everyday word for soured feeling, at any depth and any duration — an afternoon's disappointment or a decade's feud. Rancor is bitterness at the far end of that range: deep, old, and durable, ill will that has soaked in and stays for years.

Acrimony is bitterness breaking out into the open — sharp words, cutting exchanges, a divorce fought line by line. Rancor does not need to speak: it can sit in silence for years and still poison a room. Acrimony is heard; rancor is kept.
